# Emergency Care System

> A public, free, open-source demonstration of how to plan an emergency
> care system, from higher-level use cases to lower-level test
> automation. All data is synthetic; this is not a real emergency care
> system.

This file follows the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) convention: a map
of this site's pages for AI agents and LLMs, kept in sync with
`static/llms.json` (same content, structured) and with
[`spec/site-architecture.md`](https://github.com/emergency-care-system/emergency-care-system.github.io/blob/main/spec/site-architecture.md)
in this site's own source repository, which is the canonical source of
truth for both files.

## Pages

- [Home](https://emergency-care-system.github.io/): overview of the demo, its 22 features, and its twelve test suites.
- [Features](https://emergency-care-system.github.io/features/): all 22 Gherkin features, each with its user story and a link to the `.feature` file.
- [Testing](https://emergency-care-system.github.io/testing/): how the same 171 scenarios are ported across Selenium/Playwright × JavaScript/TypeScript/Python/C#/Java/Rust.
- [About](https://emergency-care-system.github.io/about/): what this demo is, what it isn't, and how the source repository is organized.

## Source repository

- [emergency-care-system/emergency-care-system](https://github.com/emergency-care-system/emergency-care-system): the app (`src/`), the specs (`spec/`), the Claude Code skills (`skills/`), and all twelve test suites.
